page: Microsoft Azure D13_v2 is a Dv2-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 50 MB L3 cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache, with support for AVX and AVX512F vector extensions. It is equipped with 56.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB per core, and includes 410 GB of local storage. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is consistently low, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression all falling into the bottom 10% of tested systems. However, multi-core execution scales to average levels, as demonstrated by middle-50% scores in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains stable in the average tier for both small cached blocks at 558.43 GB/sec and large uncached blocks at 68.53 GB/sec read and 39.53 GB/sec write.

The instance is suited for workloads that benefit from a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and multi-threaded processing, such as database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, which all achieved average benchmark ratings. Conversely, it is poorly suited for single-threaded tasks or intensive language model inference, where text generation speeds for 135M and 7B models fall into the bottom 25%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D13_v2 offers a dense memory allocation and substantial local storage on legacy hardware, making it a viable option for memory-bound applications that do not require high single-threaded CPU throughput.
